messages:
Chris (infra): Heads up — saw a ~$38k billing bump between 02:00-03:00 UTC. Looks like autoscaler launched ~30 on-demand g5.12x instances instead of our reserved g4dn-8x pool.
Amanda L: OMG :facepalm: any idea why it picked g5? our provisioner selector should be compute-optimized.
Chris (infra): Quick dumps: kubectl shows nodes with unexpected instanceType. Snippet I ran: ```
kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep 'node-1|node-2|node-3'
node-177   Ready   12d   10.10.2.5   g5.12xlarge
node-178   Ready   11d   10.10.2.6   g5.12xlarge
```
Julio R: I dug into the TF state — last apply accidentally overwrote the provisioner mapping. `cloudInstanceClass: default-gpu` got changed to `default-gpu: mem-optimized` in the module, which maps to a2-highmem/a2-mega (no commitment). Autoscaler falls back to whatever family the selector resolves to -> on-demand.
Amanda L: So the committed usage % dropped during the window? that would explain the extra charges.
Chris (infra): Yes — committed coverage dropped to ~62% for the GPU family in us-west1 during the spike. Provider only applies discounts to exact family+region matches.
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert generated: billing-anomaly-1767123456. Creating support ticket BU-12345 with provider.
Amanda L: I opened the cloud support ticket (BU-12345) and attached the line-item export. Filing for a credit. Link: https://console.cloud/billing/export/BU-12345.csv
Julio R: Remediation steps I ran: disabled autoscaler for that pool, cordoned + drained the runaway nodes: `kubectl cordon node-177 && kubectl drain node-177 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then rolled back the TF change to restore `default-gpu: compute-optimized`. Nodes terminated and replacement came from reserved pool.
Chris (infra): Confirmed scale down and replacements in logs. Next: audit the commit that changed mapping. Commands to check: `terraform state show module.provisioner.aws_launch_template.gpu` and `git log -n 5 -- terraform/modules/provisioner`.
Amanda L: Preliminary finance calc: roughly 28 node-hours of on-demand * differential ≈ $29k excess. Submitted estimate in BU-12345. Finance looped in.
SRE Pager: Noted we also hit reserved-pool soft quota earlier (spiky allocation) which made autoscaler prefer noncommitted fallback in that AZ. Need to verify if quota exhaustion or pure misconfig was dominant.
Chris (infra): Action items: 1) Julio to revert TF commit + add a plan-time guard that rejects any instanceClass->family mapping that isn't in the committed list (PR + unit test). 2) Amanda to own the provider ticket and credit request. 3) Ops to add an alert that fires when instanceType of newly created nodes != expected family label. 4) Add runbook section: emergency scale-down for runaway GPU launches.
Julio R: I'll open the PR now and add a terraform plan-time check. tagging @Chris (please review).
Amanda L: Also recommending a hard cap on on-demand pool size so a single bug can't exhaust budget. I'll add to the ticket and infra roadmap.
Chris (infra): Agree. Added a card to infra board and set assignees. Please post status updates in BU-12345. Closing note: once billing credit confirmed, we'll run a postmortem + follow-ups. :thumbsup:
